name: OWASP NodeGoat

license.note: LICENSE at the pinned commit is the Apache License 2.0 text (the appendix copyright placeholder is unfilled, as in the stock template). README.md says 'Code licensed under the Apache License v2.0' and package.json has the license field 'Apache 2.0'. Source is fetched at run time and never vendored. No other licensing question found.

bootNotes: docker-compose.yml starts a mongo:4.4 service and runs artifacts/db-reset.js before npm start, so no separate seed hint is given. NODE_ENV is left unset (defaults to development); NodeGoat has no config for a 'synthetic' environment, and compose supplies MONGODB_URI itself, so env is empty.

labels.title: NoSQL (MongoDB $where) injection via the threshold query parameter
labels.notes: This is the gate case. The sink is a MongoDB $where JavaScript expression built by template string from req.query.threshold. It is NoSQL injection, not SQL. fixtures/casefiles/nodegoat-sqli-001.json names it sql-concat and gives range 70-74, which does not match the pinned source (the commented-out upstream fix occupies lines 63-76).

labels.title: Server-side JavaScript injection via eval of request body fields
labels.notes: eval(req.body.preTax), afterTax and roth. Source and sink are the same lines.

labels.title: Log injection: unauthenticated userName written to the log without CRLF encoding
labels.notes: console.log of req.body.userName for an unknown user lets an attacker forge log lines with CR or LF. Upstream tutorial item A1-3. The commented-out fix is at lines 66-80.

labels.title: Insecure direct object reference: allocations looked up by URL userId, not session
labels.notes: Any logged-in user can read another user's allocations by changing :userId. The upstream fix (commented out at lines 12-15) reads userId from req.session.

labels.title: Missing function-level access control: benefits updated for any userId in the body
labels.notes: Upstream classes this as A7 (missing function-level access control). It is labeled idor because the contracts VulnClass has only injection and idor and the exploit is a user-supplied userId with no ownership or role check (the isAdmin variant is commented out in app/routes/index.js lines 55-60).

safeVariants.notes: One-line change: the threshold is coerced with parseInt(threshold, 10) and interpolated as a number, so it can only be an integer or NaN. Numeric thresholds behave as before; a non-numeric value yields NaN and matches nothing. A string can no longer break out of the quoted literal. The other labeled issues are deliberately left unpatched, so this variant closes only the gate issue.

negativeControls.whyNotExploitable: countHighStockAllocations builds a $where expression with a template string, which an injection rule matches, but the only interpolated value is the module constant HIGH_STOCK_PERCENT = 50. No request data reaches it and nothing in the app calls it, so no witness can make it pass. The patches apply in order: the safe variant first (so the tree has no live injection at the gate site), then the control. The rule id is the planned L1-04 rule name, not yet implemented.

outOfScope.issue: Cross-site scripting, CSRF, weak session and cookie settings, weak password storage, open redirect and SSRF items from the NodeGoat tutorial
outOfScope.reason: VulnClass in contracts v1.0 is injection or idor only, so these have no class to be labeled under in this phase. They are not claimed to be absent.

outOfScope.issue: Other handlers (profile, memos, research) beyond the sinks labeled here
outOfScope.reason: Not selected for the first pair; add labels when a rule or witness needs them.
